title: Playing for white audiences, treatment and pay
summary: The band mostly played white jobs, was treated well, and was paid well; a patron paid Buddy generously.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In Covenant. Was that for colored people?
Did you mainly play for white people, or did you play?

We played more white jobs than we did colored jobs. Really? Yeah. I'm surprised to hear that. Yeah, yeah. We had lots of jobs, like I told you. All around Campwood, Louisiana. All true that, you know, that I see that we played different places over there, and, uh, that's why a buddy got such a big, you know, a big name like he did. Bubba Lewis had always been Bubba. He used to play for the male. The male used to give dances over there all the time. Uh-huh.

Oh, yeah, yeah, them people. Well, I mean, you didn't have, uh, you know, I mean, none of that good liquor like they had, no, they got that, uh, what's called alcohol, you know? Well, that's the most, they were selling at that time, where they'd bring that stuff on there, and give it to the boys, you know? But boys treated you nice, they treated you like you was a musician. Oh. Yeah.
I mean, did they have any sort of racial, um, problems or anything like that?
You take, you know, like that neighborhood up there now, you know, up around Barcaloosa and all, I mean, I don't know how you feel, but I wouldn't like to go out there too much.

No. Well, it wasn't like that at that time. Everybody didn't know their place, you know what I mean? You go in your place, and they go in their place, and that's the way they got along like that. It wasn't no humbug at all out there, because the white people were just as, you know, glad to have the colored band to play for them, and to have the white band, which they didn't have no white band out there at that time, you know? And that's why they used to catch Buddy all the time. And when we'd be waiting for the man, would he come get us? You know, they sent a big old truck to get us and bring us back. Go out there, feed you, and, you know, give you money. Last time, you, you, Bubba used to go out there and get money and wouldn't be working, you know? He said, well, I'm going out to Bubba Luce. He was staying in the club. He'd go out there and get forty, fifty dollars from the man all the time. He disliked the band so much, though, he would have did anything for the band. The man, that was? The man of Bubba Luce.
How much would you get paid for a job then?
Well, the job wasn't so hot. You'd make four or five hours, you know. Well, it was money at that time. Yeah, right.
